name: GATE CSE (Computer Science & IT)
conductedBy: IISc Bengaluru & seven IITs on behalf of the Ministry of Education (GATE 2027: IIT Madras)
tagline: Gateway to M.Tech/MS/PhD at IITs, IISc & NITs and to PSU jobs

overview.about: The Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) is a national computer-based exam for engineering and science graduates. The CS paper tests engineering mathematics and core computer science; scores are used for postgraduate admissions, scholarships and recruitment by several PSUs. The organising institute rotates each year — GATE 2026 was run by IIT Guwahati and GATE 2027 by IIT Madras.
eligibility: Students in the third or higher year of an undergraduate degree, or graduates (B.E./B.Tech/B.Sc (4-yr)/M.Sc/MCA and others as listed in the brochure)
A candidate may take one paper or two papers from the permitted combinations
Check the current year's information brochure on the official GATE site

pattern.note: MCQ: −1/3 (1-mark), −2/3 (2-mark); no negative marking for MSQ and NAT

overview.frequency: Once a year (computer-based test in February); score valid for 3 years

cards.title: Rank
cards.body: Rank = maximum number of linearly independent rows (= columns). Row-reduce to echelon form and count non-zero rows. rank(A) ≤ min(m, n).

cards.title: Solving Ax = b
points: Unique solution iff that rank = number of unknowns n
Ax = 0 always has the trivial solution; non-trivial iff rank < n

cards.title: Eigenvalue shortcuts
points: Triangular matrix: eigenvalues are the diagonal entries
Aᵏ has eigenvalues λᵏ; A⁻¹ has 1/λ; A + kI has λ + k

cards.title: Symmetric matrices
cards.body: Real symmetric matrices have real eigenvalues, and eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal. Skew-symmetric matrices have purely imaginary (or zero) eigenvalues.

cards.title: Determinant rules
points: det(kA) = kⁿ det(A) for n × n
Swapping two rows flips the sign

cards.q: A 3 × 3 matrix has eigenvalues 1, 2 and 3. det(A²) = ?

cards.explain: Row 2 = 2 × Row 1; rows 1 and 3 are independent.

cards.q: For a 3 × 3 system with rank(A) = 2 and rank([A | b]) = 3, the system has:
cards.explain: Unequal ranks mean the system is inconsistent.

cards.title: Conditional probability & Bayes
points: Bayes: P(A | B) = P(B | A) P(A) / P(B)
Total probability: P(B) = Σ P(B | Aᵢ) P(Aᵢ)

cards.title: Bayes in action
cards.body: Disease prevalence 1%, test sensitivity 99%, false-positive rate 5%. P(+) = 0.0099 + 0.0495 = 0.0594. P(D | +) = 0.0099 / 0.0594 = 1/6 ≈ 0.167.

cards.title: Expectation & variance
cards.body: E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y] always (linearity, even if dependent). Var(X) = E[X²] − (E[X])². Var(aX + b) = a² Var(X).

cards.title: Standard distributions
points: Binomial(n, p): mean np, variance np(1 − p)
Uniform(a, b): mean (a + b)/2, variance (b − a)²/12

cards.title: Geometric waiting
cards.body: Expected number of rolls of a fair die to get the first 6: p = 1/6, so 1/p = 6 rolls.

cards.title: Calculus essentials
cards.body: Use L'Hôpital for 0/0 or ∞/∞ limits. Critical points where f′(x) = 0: f″ < 0 → local max, f″ > 0 → local min. Check endpoints on closed intervals.

cards.q: Expected value of the sum of two fair dice:
Variance of a Uniform(0, 1) random variable:
Maximum value of f(x) = x(4 − x) over real x:
cards.explain: f′(x) = 4 − 2x = 0 → x = 2, f(2) = 4; f″ = −2 < 0, so it is a maximum.

cards.title: Propositional logic
points: Contrapositive ¬q → ¬p is equivalent; converse q → p is not
Tautology: true for all assignments; check with a truth table or by contradiction

cards.title: Quantifiers
cards.body: ¬∀x P(x) ≡ ∃x ¬P(x) and ¬∃x P(x) ≡ ∀x ¬P(x). ∀x∃y is not the same as ∃y∀x — order matters.

cards.title: Relation properties
cards.body: Reflexive, symmetric, antisymmetric, transitive. Equivalence = reflexive + symmetric + transitive. Partial order = reflexive + antisymmetric + transitive.

cards.title: Counting relations on an n-element set
Counting functions from A (|A| = n) to B (|B| = m)
points: Onto: by inclusion–exclusion Σ (−1)ᵏ C(m, k)(m − k)ⁿ

cards.title: Groups
cards.body: A group needs closure, associativity, identity and inverses. Lagrange: the order of a subgroup divides the order of the group. Every group of prime order is cyclic.

cards.q: Number of reflexive relations on a 3-element set:
Which is logically equivalent to p → q?
Number of functions from a 3-element set to a 2-element set:

cards.title: Degrees & trees
cards.body: Handshaking: Σ deg(v) = 2|E|, so the number of odd-degree vertices is even. A tree on n vertices has n − 1 edges; Cayley: nⁿ⁻² labelled trees on n vertices.

cards.title: Euler & Hamilton
cards.body: Euler circuit: connected and every vertex has even degree. Euler path: exactly 0 or 2 odd-degree vertices. Hamiltonian cycle has no simple characterisation (NP-complete).

cards.title: Colouring
cards.body: Chromatic number: bipartite graphs 2 (if at least one edge), Kₙ needs n, odd cycle needs 3, any planar graph ≤ 4.

cards.title: Counting tools
points: Pigeonhole: n + 1 objects in n boxes → some box has 2
Catalan Cₙ = (2n)! / ((n + 1)! n!): BST shapes, valid bracket sequences

cards.title: Catalan check
cards.body: C₁ = 1, C₂ = 2, C₃ = 5, C₄ = 14. So 3 distinct keys form 5 different BSTs.

cards.q: Number of labelled trees on 4 vertices:
Maximum edges in a simple planar graph with 10 vertices:
Number of structurally distinct BSTs with 3 distinct keys:

cards.title: Boolean laws
points: De Morgan: (AB)′ = A′ + B′, (A + B)′ = A′B′
Consensus: AB + A′C + BC = AB + A′C

cards.title: K-maps
cards.body: Group adjacent 1s in powers of two (1, 2, 4, 8), as large as possible, wrapping around edges. Use don't-cares (X) only when they enlarge a group.

cards.title: Minimise
cards.body: F(A, B, C) = Σm(0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7). Minterms 0–3 are A′ (a group of 4); 1, 3, 5, 7 are C (a group of 4). F = A′ + C.

cards.title: Universal gates
cards.body: NAND and NOR can each build any circuit. XOR needs 4 NAND gates (minimum); NOT from NAND: tie both inputs together.

cards.title: 2's complement
cards.body: n bits represent −2ⁿ⁻¹ to 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1. Overflow happens when adding two numbers of the same sign gives a result of the opposite sign.

cards.title: Combinational blocks
cards.body: A 2ⁿ:1 MUX implements any n-variable function (n select lines). Full adder: Sum = A ⊕ B ⊕ Cin, Carry = AB + Cin(A ⊕ B).

cards.title: Sequential circuits
cards.body: Flip-flops are edge-triggered; latches are level-sensitive. D: Q⁺ = D. T: Q⁺ = T ⊕ Q. JK: Q⁺ = JQ′ + K′Q. n flip-flops give a mod-2ⁿ ripple counter.

cards.q: Range of an 8-bit 2's complement integer:
Minimum number of 2-input NAND gates to implement XOR:
cards.explain: The standard 4-NAND XOR circuit is minimal.

cards.q: F(A, B, C) = Σm(0, 2, 4, 6) simplifies to:
cards.explain: All four minterms have C = 0 and every combination of A, B.

cards.title: Pipelining
points: k stages, n instructions, no stalls: (k + n − 1) cycles
Cycle time = slowest stage + latch delay

cards.title: Hazards
cards.body: Structural (resource conflict), data (RAW — fixed by forwarding or stalls), control (branches — prediction, delayed branch). Load-use hazards still need one stall with forwarding.

cards.title: Cache performance
points: AMAT = hit time + miss rate × miss penalty
Hierarchical: Tavg = H·Tc + (1 − H)(Tc + Tm) if checked sequentially

cards.title: Cache mapping
cards.body: Address = tag | index | block offset. Direct-mapped: index selects a line. k-way set-associative: index selects a set. Fully associative: no index bits.

cards.title: Address split
cards.body: 32-bit address, 16 KB direct-mapped cache, 64 B blocks. Offset = 6 bits; lines = 16 KB / 64 B = 256 → index 8 bits; tag = 32 − 8 − 6 = 18 bits.

cards.title: I/O
cards.body: Programmed I/O polls, interrupt-driven I/O frees the CPU between transfers, DMA transfers whole blocks with CPU involvement only at start and end.

cards.q: A 5-stage pipeline executes 100 instructions with no stalls. Cycles needed:
Hit time 1 ns, miss rate 5%, miss penalty 100 ns. AMAT = ?
32-bit address, 16 KB direct-mapped cache, 64-byte blocks. Tag bits:

cards.title: C parameter passing
cards.body: C is strictly call-by-value; passing a pointer lets the callee modify the caller's object. A swap(int a, int b) that swaps its parameters changes nothing in the caller.

cards.title: Scope and storage
cards.body: C uses static (lexical) scoping. static locals persist across calls; automatic locals are re-created each call. Watch for dangling pointers to returned locals.

cards.title: Array address (row-major)
points: A[i][j] in an R × C array: base + (i·C + j) × size
Adjust i, j if the lower bound isn't 0

cards.title: Binary tree facts
cards.body: In any binary tree, leaves = (nodes with two children) + 1. A binary tree with n nodes has n + 1 NULL child pointers.

cards.title: Heaps
cards.body: Array storage: children of i at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2 (0-indexed). Insert and delete-min O(log n). Building a heap bottom-up from n elements is O(n), not O(n log n).

cards.title: Hashing
cards.body: Chaining keeps lists per slot; open addressing probes (linear → primary clustering; quadratic; double hashing). Expected chain length = load factor α = n/m.

cards.q: int A[10][20] (4-byte ints, row-major) starts at address 1000. Address of A[2][3]:
A binary tree has 10 leaves. How many nodes have exactly two children?
Time to build a binary heap from n unsorted elements (bottom-up heapify):
cards.explain: Most nodes are near the leaves and sift down only a little; the sum is linear.

cards.title: Master theorem: T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n)
points: f(n) = O(n^(log_b a − ε)) → Θ(n^(log_b a))
f(n) = Θ(n^(log_b a)) → Θ(n^(log_b a) log n)
f(n) = Ω(n^(log_b a + ε)) + regularity → Θ(f(n))

cards.title: Apply it
cards.body:
T(n) = 4T(n/2) + n: n^(log₂4) = n² dominates → Θ(n²).
T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n: equal → Θ(n log n).

cards.title: Greedy algorithms
cards.body: Activity selection (earliest finish), fractional knapsack (value/weight), Huffman coding, Kruskal and Prim MSTs, Dijkstra. Greedy fails for 0/1 knapsack.

cards.title: DP complexities
points: LCS of lengths m, n: O(mn)

cards.title: Lower bounds
cards.body: Any comparison sort needs Ω(n log n) comparisons in the worst case. Finding both max and min of n elements needs ⌈3n/2⌉ − 2 comparisons.

cards.title: Graph algorithm costs
cards.body: BFS/DFS O(V + E); Dijkstra with binary heap O((V + E) log V); Prim with heap O(E log V); Kruskal O(E log E). DFS classifies tree, back, forward and cross edges; a back edge means a cycle.

cards.q: T(n) = 8T(n/2) + n² solves to:
Minimum scalar multiplications for A(10×20), B(20×30), C(30×40):
Minimum comparisons to find both max and min of 100 elements:

cards.title: Chomsky hierarchy
cards.body: Regular ⊂ context-free ⊂ context-sensitive ⊂ recursive ⊂ recursively enumerable. Machines: DFA/NFA, PDA, LBA, Turing machine (halting deciders for recursive).

cards.title: Finite automata
cards.body: DFA and NFA accept the same languages; subset construction can need up to 2ⁿ states. Minimise a DFA by merging equivalent states. 'Number mod k' languages need k states.

cards.title: Pumping lemma
cards.body: Used to prove non-regularity: aⁿbⁿ, palindromes, {a^p : p prime} are not regular. For CFLs: aⁿbⁿcⁿ and {ww} are not context-free.

cards.title: Closure properties
points: Regular: union, intersection, complement, concatenation, star, reversal, homomorphism
CFL: union, concatenation, star — NOT intersection or complement
DCFL: closed under complement, not union
Recursive: closed under complement; RE: not

cards.title: Decidability
points: Decidable: membership, emptiness, finiteness for CFGs; equivalence of DFAs
Undecidable: halting problem, equivalence of CFGs, ambiguity of a CFG, whether a CFG generates Σ*
Rice's theorem: any non-trivial property of the language of a TM is undecidable

cards.title: DFA for divisibility
cards.body: Binary numbers (MSB first) divisible by 3: states are remainders 0, 1, 2. On bit b, r → (2r + b) mod 3. Start and accept at 0 → 3 states.

cards.q: Which language is NOT context-free?
cards.explain: A single stack cannot match three counts.

cards.q: States in the minimal DFA accepting binary numbers divisible by 5:
cards.explain: One state per remainder 0–4, all distinguishable.

cards.q: Which problem is undecidable?
options: Membership of a string in a CFL
cards.explain: CFG equivalence is undecidable; the others have algorithms.

cards.title: Phases
cards.body: Lexical analysis → syntax analysis → semantic analysis → intermediate code → optimisation → code generation. The symbol table is shared by all phases.

cards.title: Counting tokens
cards.body:
printf("%d", x);
Tokens: printf ( "%d" , x ) ; → 7. A string literal is one token; whitespace and comments are not tokens.

cards.title: Top-down parsing
cards.body: LL(1) needs a grammar free of left recursion and left-factored, with disjoint FIRST sets per alternative (and FIRST/FOLLOW disjoint when ε is derivable).

cards.title: Bottom-up parsing
cards.body: Power: LR(0) < SLR(1) < LALR(1) < CLR(1). LALR merges CLR states with the same core, so it has as many states as LR(0)/SLR; merging can create reduce–reduce conflicts. YACC builds LALR(1).

cards.title: Syntax-directed translation
cards.body: S-attributed: only synthesised attributes, evaluated bottom-up. L-attributed: inherited attributes depend only on the parent and left siblings — evaluable in one left-to-right pass.

cards.title: Intermediate code & blocks
cards.body: Three-address code (quadruples, triples), SSA form. Leaders: first instruction, any jump target, and the instruction after a jump. Each leader starts a basic block.

cards.q: Number of tokens in: int a = b + 10;
YACC generates which kind of parser?
cards.explain: YACC/Bison build LALR(1) tables by default.

cards.q: Which must be eliminated before building an LL(1) parser?
cards.explain: Left recursion makes a top-down parser loop forever.

cards.title: fork() counting
cards.body: Each fork() doubles the number of processes. A loop calling fork() n times creates 2ⁿ processes in total (2ⁿ − 1 children). A printf after the loop runs 2ⁿ times.

cards.title: Scheduling metrics
points: SRTF minimises average waiting time (given known bursts)

cards.title: Critical-section requirements
cards.body: Mutual exclusion, progress, bounded waiting. Peterson's solution meets all three for 2 processes. Semaphores: wait/P decrements (blocks if < 0), signal/V increments.

cards.title: Deadlock resource bound
points: n processes, each needs at most k units:
Minimum units guaranteeing no deadlock = n(k − 1) + 1
Banker's algorithm checks for a safe sequence before granting

cards.title: Paging numbers
points: Pages = virtual space / page size; page table size = pages × PTE size
EAT with TLB (hit ratio h, single-level): h(t + m) + (1 − h)(t + 2m)

cards.title: Page replacement & disks
cards.body: FIFO (Belady's anomaly possible), LRU, Optimal. Disk scheduling: FCFS, SSTF (starvation), SCAN/elevator, C-SCAN, LOOK/C-LOOK — count head movement carefully.

cards.title: Page-table size
cards.body: 32-bit virtual address, 4 KB pages → 2³² / 2¹² = 2²⁰ pages. With 4-byte entries: 2²⁰ × 4 B = 4 MB per process — the reason multilevel page tables exist.

cards.q: 3 processes each need up to 4 units of a resource. Minimum units that guarantee no deadlock:
TLB hit ratio 80%, TLB access 10 ns, memory access 100 ns, single-level paging. EAT = ?
for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) fork(); — total processes including the original:

cards.title: Relational algebra
cards.body: σ (select rows), π (project columns, removes duplicates), ⋈ (join), ∪, −, ×, ρ (rename), ÷ (division for 'for all' queries).

cards.title: SQL subtleties
cards.body: Comparisons with NULL give UNKNOWN, so WHERE x = NULL matches nothing; use IS NULL. COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(col) skips NULLs. NOT IN with a NULL in the subquery returns no rows.

cards.title: Functional dependencies
cards.body: Compute attribute closure X⁺ by repeatedly applying FDs. X is a super key if X⁺ = all attributes; a candidate key if also minimal. Armstrong's axioms: reflexivity, augmentation, transitivity.

cards.title: Find all candidate keys
cards.body: R(A, B, C, D), F = {AB → C, C → D, D → A}. B is on no right side, so every key contains B. AB⁺ = ABCD, BC⁺ = BCDA, BD⁺ = BDAC; B⁺ = B. Keys: AB, BC, BD.

cards.title: Decomposition
cards.body: Lossless if the common attributes form a key of at least one part. 3NF decomposition can always be lossless and dependency-preserving; BCNF is always lossless but may lose dependencies.

cards.title: Serialisability
cards.body: Draw the precedence graph from conflicting operations (RW, WR, WW on the same item by different transactions). Acyclic ⇒ conflict serialisable. Basic 2PL guarantees conflict serialisability but not freedom from deadlock.

cards.title: Recoverability
cards.body: Recoverable: a transaction commits only after those it read from commit. Cascadeless: read only committed data. Strict: no read or write of uncommitted data. Strict ⊂ cascadeless ⊂ recoverable.

cards.q: R(A, B, C, D) with F = {AB → C, C → D, D → A}. How many candidate keys?
Basic two-phase locking (2PL) guarantees:
cards.explain: 2PL ensures serialisability; deadlocks are still possible.

cards.title: Subnetting & CIDR
cards.body: A /p prefix leaves 32 − p host bits: 2^(32−p) addresses, 2^(32−p) − 2 usable hosts. Routers forward using longest-prefix match.

cards.title: TCP congestion control
cards.body: Slow start: cwnd doubles each RTT until ssthresh. Congestion avoidance: +1 MSS per RTT. On timeout: ssthresh = cwnd/2, cwnd = 1 MSS. On 3 duplicate ACKs (Reno): fast retransmit, cwnd halves.

cards.title: Error control
points: Minimum Hamming distance d: detect up to d − 1 errors
CRC: append r bits where the generator has degree r

cards.title: CSMA/CD
points: Minimum frame size = 2 × propagation delay × bandwidth

cards.title: Routing
cards.body: Distance vector (Bellman–Ford, neighbours exchange vectors, count-to-infinity problem; RIP). Link state (flooded LSAs, each router runs Dijkstra; OSPF).

cards.title: Headers & ports
cards.body: IPv4 header 20–60 bytes; TCP header 20–60 bytes; UDP header 8 bytes. DNS over UDP 53, HTTP 80, HTTPS 443, SMTP 25.

cards.q: A code has minimum Hamming distance 5. It can correct up to:
Maximum Go-Back-N sender window with 3-bit sequence numbers:
CSMA/CD at 10 Mbps with 25.6 µs one-way propagation delay. Minimum frame size:

cards.title: What GA is
cards.body: 10 questions worth 15 marks (5 × 1 mark + 5 × 2 marks), common to all GATE papers. These are the easiest marks in the exam — never skip GA practice.

cards.title: Four areas
points: Verbal: grammar, vocabulary, sentence completion, analogies
Quantitative: percentages, ratios, data interpretation, mensuration
Spatial: rotation, folding, paper cutting, mirror images

cards.title: Quant sample
cards.body: Boys : girls = 3 : 2 (take 60 and 40). 20% of boys and 30% of girls hold scholarships: 12 + 12 = 24. So 76% do not.

cards.title: Clock angle
points: Take 360 − angle if the result exceeds 180 for the smaller angle

cards.title: Painted cube
cards.body: A painted n × n × n cube is cut into unit cubes: 3 faces painted = 8 (corners), 2 faces = 12(n − 2), 1 face = 6(n − 2)², none = (n − 2)³.

cards.title: Time plan
cards.body: Do GA first in about 15–20 minutes; the NAT and MSQ items there have no negative marking, so answer every one.

cards.q: Angle between the hands of a clock at 3:15:
A painted 3 × 3 × 3 cube is cut into 27 unit cubes. How many have exactly two painted faces?
Boys:girls = 3:2; 20% of boys and 30% of girls have scholarships. Percentage without scholarship:
cards.explain: Of 100 students, 12 + 12 = 24 have one, so 76% don't.
